display_heading.headline: Back To The Front
display_heading.deck: In The 1936 Play Idiot's Delight, An Assortment Of Characters Meet In An Alpine Hotel As The Storm Clouds Of War Gather Around Them

contact_edits.before: The upper half of the set, representing his bedroom, has been turned at an angle of 90 degrees, prompting physical feats and scenic images that recall Robert Lepage's Needles and Opium and, less expectedly, the opening number of Hairspray. Some of the family scenes go on too long, and analogies to Nazism are pushed too hard (Idiot's Delight in reverse), but this is a superb - well, a transformative - production. Weekend Post robert.cushman@hotmail.com
